sections.html: A tetra from Peru that has been popular among aquarists since 1958 under the fantasy name "Hyphessobrycon robertsi". Males like to impress each other with their enormously extended dorsal fins, which led to the German common name "Sichelsalmler" (sickle tetra).

For a long time the species was not scientifically named. In a study on the relationship of the "rosy tetras", to which the robertsi-tetra belongs, Stanley Weitzman and Lisa Palmer assumed in 1997 that the animals were the same species as Hyphessobrycon bentosi.

In 2014 Axel Zarske of the Senckenberg Museum presented a new study identifying differences between Hyphessobrycon bentosi and the robertsi-tetra. He concluded that they are different species and described the robertsi-tetra with the valid name Hyphessobrycon jackrobertsi. With this, Zarske honours the discoverer of the species, Jack Roberts from Miami, who was already meant by the invalid name "robertsi".

Young adult wild specimens of the species are available again. The type specimens for the first description of H. jackrobertsi also originated from the same fish house.
